dedupe_keys.name: atsc 3 0 broadcast standards and a 326 field test plan

description: ATSC 3.0 is the internet-protocol based digital television broadcast standard used in the United States (as NextGen TV), South Korea and other countries, and the Advanced Television Systems Committee publishes its full specification suite free of charge. The suite runs from A/300 (system overview) through the physical layer (A/322), studio-to-transmitter link (A/324), link layer (A/330), signalling, delivery and synchronisation (A/331), service announcement and usage reporting, watermarks, companion devices, video, audio and captions, and A/200 on regional service availability. The companion A/326 ATSC 3.0 Field Test Plan (2024 edition) standardises how broadcasters measure coverage, service reception and channel characteristics, including single frequency networks, for fixed outdoor, fixed indoor, portable, pedestrian and mobile reception; it defines site selection, test vehicles, the measurement data set to record, procedures and analysis, so that field campaigns can be compared and used to calibrate coverage predictions. Coverage: countries adopting ATSC 3.0; documents dated from 2016 to 2026, with most current editions from April 2026. Format and access: PDF downloads from the ATSC website, free; no open licence stated. Caveats: the documents are specifications, not measurement data; field test results are published separately by broadcasters and are not collected here. Simulation uses: parameters for coverage and service models of broadcast networks, calibration of propagation predictions against standardised measurements, and emergency alerting capabilities (advanced emergency information) in digital twins of broadcast systems. Related records: the DVB-T2 specification is the European counterpart, and the FCC LMS database holds US station parameters.
